items.question: What evidence indicates the cultivation of cotton in the Indus Valley Civilisation?
items.answer: The discovery of woven cotton textile fragments at Mohenjo-daro and traces of cotton seeds. The Greeks called cotton sindon, derived from the word 'Sindhu' (Indus).

items.question: Describe the mathematical ratio used in the Harappan weight system.
items.answer: For lower denominations, weights followed a binary system (1, 2, 4, 8, 16, 32, 64), while higher values transitioned into a decimal system (160, 200, 320, 640, 1600, 3200, etc.), with a unit weight of approx. 13.63g.

items.question: Where is the earliest and most direct evidence of canal irrigation found?
items.answer: At Shortughai in northern Afghanistan, though generally canal irrigation was rare inside the main alluvial plains, where agriculture relied on seasonal floodwater and wells.

items.question: Which two sites were dedicated centers for the manufacture of shell objects?
items.answer: Balakot and Nageshwar. Both are coastal sites rich in marine shells, specializing in making bangles, ladles, and inlay pieces.

items.question: Which cuneiform term refers to the Indus region, and how is its trade described?
items.answer: Mesopotamian texts refer to the Indus region as Meluhha, describing it as a land of exotic timbers, carnelian, lapis lazuli, gold, and copper, whose ships docked at Akkad.

sections.title: 1. Agriculture and Animal Husbandry
sections.content:
The urban structure of Harappan towns was sustained by a robust agricultural surplus generated in rural hinterlands, using innovative farming and water management systems.

Crops & Agricultural Technology
  • Principal Crops: Wheat, barley, peas, lentils, mustard, sesame, and chickpeas. Rice husks have been recovered from Lothal and Rangpur, showing localized cultivation.
  • Cotton: The Harappans were the first in the world to cultivate cotton (Greek: Sindon), which was exported to the West.
  • Tillage Evidence: A ploughed field showing grid furrows (double-cropping pattern of mustard and horse gram/peas) was excavated at Kalibangan. Terracotta models of ploughs have been recovered from Banawali (Haryana) and Jawaiwala (Pakistan).
Irrigation, Water Storage & Livestock
  • Irrigation: Direct traces of canals are found at Shortughai (Afghanistan). In the plains, alluvial inundation and well irrigation (like the public wells at Mohenjo-daro) were mainstays. Gabarbands (stone dams) in Baluchistan collected slope runoff.
  • Water Reservoirs: Dholavira features massive stone-cut reservoirs to store rainwater, indicating sophisticated dryland water management.
  • Animal Husbandry: Domestication of humped cattle (zebu), sheep, goats, pigs, buffaloes, asses, and camels. Humped bulls were highly revered.
  • The Horse Controversy: Horse bones have been reported at Surkotada (Gujarat), but horse depictions are absent on Harappan seals and pottery. The animal was not a central part of Harappan socio-economic life.

masteryZone.q: Which of the following Mature Harappan sites has yielded the most direct evidence of a ploughed field showing grid furrows?
masteryZone.sol: Kalibangan in Rajasthan has yielded a ploughed field with grid-patterned furrows.

masteryZone.q: Direct traces of Harappan canals used for irrigation have been discovered at which site?
masteryZone.sol: Direct traces of canals are found at Shortughai in northern Afghanistan.

masteryZone.q: Which of the following crops were cultivated by the Harappans? (Select all that apply)
masteryZone.sol: Wheat, barley, peas, mustard, sesame, and lentils were cultivated. Sugar cane was not cultivated.

masteryZone.q: Select the animals domesticated by the Harappans: (Select all that apply)
masteryZone.sol: Humped cattle, buffaloes, camels, and asses were domesticated. They knew Indian elephants, not African ones.

masteryZone.q: Identify the water management structures used in Harappan agriculture: (Select all that apply)
masteryZone.sol: Reservoirs at Dholavira, Gabarbands in Baluchistan, and wells were used. Iron was unknown.

masteryZone.q: Which of the following sites in Gujarat have yielded evidence of rice cultivation? (Select all that apply)
masteryZone.sol: Lothal and Rangpur have yielded rice husks embedded in pottery clay.

masteryZone.q: Which wild animals are represented in Harappan bone assemblages and seals? (Select all that apply)
masteryZone.sol: Deer, boar, rhino, elephant, and leopard are all represented in Harappan art and bone remains.

masteryZone.q: The Harappans were the first in the world to cultivate cotton.
masteryZone.sol: True. Cotton traces are found at Mohenjo-daro, dating back to 3000 BCE.

masteryZone.q: Canal irrigation was widespread throughout the alluvial plains of Sindh.
masteryZone.sol: False. Traces of canals are absent in the main Indus plain; only found at Shortughai.

masteryZone.q: A double-ploughed agricultural field has been excavated at Kalibangan.
masteryZone.sol: True. The field features two sets of furrows at right angles to each other.

masteryZone.q: Humped cattle (zebu) were highly revered and frequently depicted on seals.
masteryZone.sol: True. The humped bull is one of the most majestic motifs on Harappan seals.

masteryZone.q: The Harappans used heavy iron ploughshares to till the black soil.
masteryZone.sol: False. Iron was unknown to the Harappans; they likely used wooden ploughs.

masteryZone.q: Rice was the primary staple crop in all northern Harappan cities.
masteryZone.sol: False. Wheat and barley were the main staples; rice was rare and localized in Gujarat.

masteryZone.q: Surkotada has yielded controversial skeletal remains of horses.
masteryZone.sol: True. Surkotada yielded horse bones, though horse representations are absent on seals.

masteryZone.q: The stone dams called Gabarbands are located in the plains of Punjab.
masteryZone.sol: False. They are found in the hilly tracts of Baluchistan.

masteryZone.q: The ploughed field excavated at Kalibangan belongs to the ___________ Harappan phase.
masteryZone.sol: The ploughed field belongs to the Early Harappan/Pre-Mature phase of Kalibangan.

masteryZone.q: Terracotta models of ploughs have been discovered at ___________ in Haryana.
masteryZone.sol: Banawali has yielded terracotta plough models.

masteryZone.q: The Greek term for cotton is ___________, derived from the word Sindhu.
masteryZone.sol: Greeks called cotton 'sindon' due to its Indus Valley origins.

masteryZone.q: Direct canal irrigation traces are found at ___________ in northern Afghanistan.
masteryZone.sol: Shortughai has clear traces of canal systems.

masteryZone.q: Stone dams built across streams to check water run-off in Baluchistan are called ___________.
masteryZone.sol: They are known as gabarbands.

masteryZone.q: Massive stone-cut reservoirs to store rainwater are characteristic of ___________.
masteryZone.sol: Dholavira is famous for its reservoirs.

masteryZone.sol: The unicorn is the most frequent motif on seals.

masteryZone.q: Why is the Kalibangan ploughed field highly significant for agricultural history?
masteryZone.sol: It shows grid furrows cutting at right angles, providing the earliest evidence of double-cropping (growing mustard and chickpea simultaneously) in antiquity.

masteryZone.q: Why did the Harappans establish reservoirs at Dholavira?
masteryZone.sol: Dholavira in the Rann of Kutch has a semi-arid climate with scarce perennial water sources. Massive stone reservoirs collected rainwater run-off to sustain the city and agriculture.

masteryZone.q: Why is the presence of the horse in the Indus Valley Civilisation controversial?
masteryZone.sol: Skeletal bones matching the horse are found at Surkotada, but horse representations are completely absent on seals and painted pottery. This suggests it was not integral to Harappan economy/culture.

masteryZone.q: How did the Harappans practice agriculture without iron tools?
masteryZone.sol: They used wooden ploughshares (indicated by terracotta models) and harvested crops using stone blades (chert) mounted on curved wooden handles or bronze sickles.

masteryZone.q: How did the Gabarbands of Baluchistan benefit dryland agriculture?
masteryZone.sol: These stone check-dams slowed down seasonal stream water, letting silt settle to create fertile soil beds and retaining water table levels for crop cultivation.

masteryZone.q: How was the grid-furrow system in Kalibangan organized to crop twice?
masteryZone.sol: The furrows ran in two directions: one set spaced closely (approx. 30 cm) for smaller crops like chickpea, and another spaced wider (approx. 1.9 m) at right angles for taller mustard plants.

masteryZone.q: Case Study: Water Scarcity and Harvesting at Dholavira. Explain its design.
masteryZone.sol: Dholavira is located on Khadir Bet island. The Harappans diverted water from two seasonal channels (Manhar and Mandsar) into a series of interconnected stone-cut reservoirs, utilizing bunds and stone masonry, creating a model for dryland urban survival.

masteryZone.q: Case Study: The Agrarian Implements of Banawali. Analyze the significance of terracotta models.
masteryZone.sol: In alluvial plains, organic wooden ploughs decay, leaving no direct trace. The recovery of baked clay models of ploughs at Banawali provided crucial proof of the shape and function of Harappan tillage tools.

masteryZone.q: Case Study: Horse Bones at Surkotada. Analyze the debates on horse domestication.
masteryZone.sol: Excavator J.P. Joshi identified horse bones in Late Mature levels. However, archaeozoologist Richard Meadow argues they might belong to the half-ass (onager) wild in Kutch. The lack of horse images on seals supports Meadow's view that the horse was not domesticated or central to IVC.

masteryZone.q: Teach the Concept: Double-Cropping Systems of the Harappans.
masteryZone.sol: Explain how the Kalibangan grid furrow pattern allowed planting two crops (mustard and chickpea) together. The crops were placed so they didn't block each other's sunlight, maximizing output in dry, rain-fed zones.

masteryZone.q: Teach the Concept: SINDON - The Origin of Cotton Cultivation.
masteryZone.sol: Explain to students that cotton was first grown and spun by Harappans around 3000 BCE. When exported to the West, Greeks named it 'Sindon', directly preserving the memory of the 'Sindhu' (Indus) River where it originated.

masteryZone.q: Teach the Concept: Inundation vs. Canal Irrigation in the Indus Plains.
masteryZone.sol: Teach the difference between Shortughai (dry region with direct canals) and the main Indus plain (which flooded annually, leaving rich silt). In the main plains, natural floods and wells were preferred over canals to prevent waterlogging.

sections.title: 2. Craft Production, Metallurgy, and Weight Systems
sections.content:
Craft specialization and state-monitored weight systems highlight the centralized quality control and industrial output of Harappan cities.

Craft Specialized Centers & Metallurgy
  • Bead-Making: Specialized workshops operated at Chanhudaro and Lothal. Processes involved drilling, heating carnelian to acquire red color, and etching designs with acid.
  • Shell-Working: Coastal specialized hubs at Nageshwar and Balakot manufactured shell bangles, ladles, and inlay work.
  • Metallurgy: Mastered copper and tin alloying to produce bronze. Copper was sourced from Khetri mines (Rajasthan) and Oman; tin was imported from Afghanistan and Central Asia. They created bronze chisels, saws, and axes. Iron was completely unknown.
Weight Standardization & Measures
  • Weights Material & Shape: Made of a fine-grained siliceous stone called chert, and were typically cubical. They were unmarked and manufactured to precise standards.
  • Weight Math: Followed a binary scale for lower denominations (1, 2, 4, 8, 16, 32, 64) and a decimal scale for higher denominations (160, 200, 320, 640, 1600, 3200, 6400, etc.). The 16th unit served as a key standard, equivalent to approx. 13.63 grams.
  • Measurement Scales: An ivory scale was discovered at Mohenjo-daro, a shell scale at Lothal, and a bronze scale at Harappa, proving standardization in linear measures.

masteryZone.q: Which of the following sites had specialized factories for bead-making, complete with drills and kilns?
masteryZone.sol: Chanhudaro and Lothal were major bead-making industrial hubs with excavated workshops.

masteryZone.q: Which of the following coastal sites specialized in manufacturing shell objects?
masteryZone.sol: Balakot and Nageshwar were coastal centers specializing in shell bangles, ladles, and inlay pieces.

masteryZone.q: What stone was primarily used to make the highly standardized Harappan cubical weights?
masteryZone.sol: Standard cubical weights were carved from chert, a fine-grained silica stone.

masteryZone.q: From which region did the Harappans procure copper to alloy with tin for bronze?
masteryZone.sol: Copper came from the Khetri mines of Rajasthan and was imported from Oman.

masteryZone.q: In the Harappan weight system, what was the approximate value of the standard unit weight (16th multiple)?
masteryZone.sol: The key unit standard weight (binary unit 16) was equivalent to approximately 13.63 grams.

masteryZone.q: Select the coastal specialized shell-working hubs of the Harappans: (Select all that apply)
masteryZone.sol: Nageshwar and Balakot are coastal sites specializing in shell objects.

masteryZone.q: Which of the following materials were utilized to manufacture Harappan weights? (Select all that apply)
masteryZone.sol: Chert, alabaster, agate, and jasper were used. Iron was unknown.

masteryZone.q: Identify the metals alloyed by Harappan smiths to produce bronze objects: (Select all that apply)
masteryZone.sol: Copper, tin, and sometimes lead were alloyed to make bronze. Zinc was not alloyed.

masteryZone.q: Which sites have yielded standardized measuring scales? (Select all that apply)
masteryZone.sol: Mohenjo-daro, Lothal, and Harappa have yielded scales of ivory, shell, and bronze respectively. No iron existed.

masteryZone.sol: Bead-making involved heating carnelian, chipping, and drilling. No iron molds existed.

masteryZone.q: Iron drills were used for perforating hard stones like carnelian.
masteryZone.sol: False. Iron was unknown. They used specialized bronze or stone (chert) drills.

masteryZone.q: Chert weights were cubical and generally lacked markings of denominations.
masteryZone.sol: True. They were polished, cubical blocks without numbers or symbols.

masteryZone.q: Tin was imported from Afghanistan and Iran to alloy copper into bronze.
masteryZone.sol: True. Tin was scarce locally and was imported from the Northwest.

masteryZone.q: The shell scale for linear measurement was discovered at Mohenjo-daro.
masteryZone.sol: False. The shell scale was found at Lothal; Mohenjo-daro yielded an ivory scale.

masteryZone.q: Copper was procured from Khetri mines of Rajasthan and also from Oman.
masteryZone.sol: True. Rajasthan and Oman were the two primary copper sources.

masteryZone.q: The Harappan weight system followed a purely binary scale for all values.
masteryZone.sol: False. Lower values were binary (up to 64), but higher values were decimal (160, 200, 320, etc.).

masteryZone.q: Chanhudaro was a major specialized craft town in Sindh.
masteryZone.sol: True. Chanhudaro was dedicated almost entirely to bead, shell, and seal craft production.

masteryZone.q: The standard unit weight of the binary system was equivalent to 13.63g.
masteryZone.sol: True. The 16th multiple weight (approx 13.63g) was the primary standard.

masteryZone.q: The stone primarily used to make standardized Harappan weights was ___________.
masteryZone.sol: Standard cubical weights were made of chert.

masteryZone.q: Coastal centers like Nageshwar and Balakot specialized in the manufacture of ___________ items.
masteryZone.sol: They specialized in shell bangles, ladles, and inlay pieces.

masteryZone.q: Bead-making factories with drills and kilns were excavated at Lothal and ___________.
masteryZone.sol: Lothal and Chanhudaro are the two premier bead hubs.

masteryZone.q: Copper was alloyed with ___________ to produce bronze.
masteryZone.sol: Copper + tin yields bronze.

masteryZone.q: An ivory scale showing standardized linear units was discovered at ___________.
masteryZone.sol: The ivory scale was found at Mohenjo-daro.

masteryZone.q: For lower values, the weight system followed a ___________ scale.
masteryZone.sol: Lower weights followed the binary scale (1, 2, 4, 8, 16, 32, 64).

masteryZone.q: For higher values, the weight system transitioned into a ___________ scale.
masteryZone.sol: Higher weights followed the decimal scale (160, 200, 320, 640...).

masteryZone.q: Chemical analyses show that Harappan copper matched the nickel impurities of copper from ___________.
masteryZone.sol: The nickel traces match copper from Oman (Makan).

masteryZone.q: Match the materials used in craft production with their typical products:

options.text: A. Cubical weights and drill bits
B. Microscopic beads and seals
C. Bangles, ladles, and decorative inlay work

masteryZone.sol: Chert is for weights; steatite for micro beads/seals; shell for bangles/inlay.

options.text: A. Mohenjo-daro scale

masteryZone.sol: Ivory scale at Mohenjo-daro; shell scale at Lothal; bronze scale at Harappa.

options.text: A. Khetri mines (Rajasthan) & Oman

masteryZone.q: Why was chert preferred over other stones for crafting Harappan weights?
masteryZone.sol: Chert is a very hard cryptocrystalline quartz. It is highly resistant to abrasion, chipping, and weathering, ensuring that the weights maintained their standardized masses over long periods of usage.

masteryZone.q: Why did the Harappan smiths alloy copper with tin to make bronze?
masteryZone.sol: Pure copper is relatively soft and dulls quickly when used for cutting. Alloying copper with 10-12% tin creates bronze, which is much harder, allows for a sharper cutting edge on tools, and flows better during casting.

masteryZone.q: Why did coastal Balakot and Nageshwar specialize in shell-craft instead of bead-making?
masteryZone.sol: These sites are located on the Arabian Sea coast, rich in marine shell beds. Proximity to raw materials made it economically efficient to specialize in shell processing and export finished shell goods inland.

masteryZone.q: How were etched carnelian beads manufactured by Harappan craftsmen?
masteryZone.sol: Raw chalcedony was heated in kilns to turn it red (converting iron to hematite). It was chipped into shape, drilled with specialized drills, etched with an alkaline paste of washing soda, and fired again to fix the white design.

masteryZone.q: How did the weight system transition mathematically from low to high denominations?
masteryZone.sol: It began with a binary scale doubling from 1 to 64. At the 16th multiple (~13.63g), it bridged into a decimal system, with higher weights being multiples like 160, 200, 320, 640, 1600, etc., up to 10,800 units.

masteryZone.q: How did scientists prove the import of Omani copper into the Indus Valley?
masteryZone.sol: Through chemical composition analysis (mass spectrometry). Both Indus copper artifacts and Omani copper ore show distinct trace levels of nickel impurities, separating them from other regional copper ores.

masteryZone.q: Case Study: Chanhudaro Craft Workshop. Describe its industrial nature.
masteryZone.sol: Chanhudaro was a tiny site (under 5 hectares) but was almost entirely devoted to craft production. Excavations revealed bead-making tools, unfinished beads, shell fragments, and seal-cutting workshops, proving it was a dedicated industrial town.

masteryZone.q: Case Study: Lothal Shell Industry. Discuss the division of labor.
masteryZone.sol: Lothal had a specialized shell workshop near the residential sectors. Raw turbinella pyrum shells were cut into bangles, and waste flakes were recycled into inlay pieces, showing structured recycling and resource efficiency.

masteryZone.q: Case Study: Weight Uniformity Across the Civilisation. Discuss its administrative implications.
masteryZone.sol: Despite covering over 1 million square kilometers, weights at Harappa, Mohenjo-daro, and Chanhu-daro conform to the exact same standard. This implies a powerful central regulatory authority enforcing commerce laws.

masteryZone.q: Teach the Concept: Bronze Smelting and Alloying Ratios in IVC.
masteryZone.sol: Teach how copper was melted and tin was added to create bronze. Highlight that the tin content in Harappan bronze tools was strictly regulated (often around 8-12%) to optimize hardness without making the metal too brittle.

masteryZone.q: Teach the Concept: The Binary-Decimal Weight System.
masteryZone.sol: Explain the mathematics of the weight system. Show how 1, 2, 4, 8, 16, 32, 64 is binary (doubling), and explain why transitioning to a decimal system (multiples of 10) was necessary for weighing large bulk merchandise.

masteryZone.q: Teach the Concept: Linear Measurement Standardization.
masteryZone.sol: Teach how the ivory scale from Mohenjo-daro features divisions equal to 1.704 mm, the smallest division recorded in the Bronze Age. Explain how this precision was used in town planning and brick manufacturing.

sections.title: 3. Trade Networks, Transport, and Maritime Communications
sections.content:
The Harappan economy relied heavily on extensive regional overland networks and international maritime trade routes connecting the Indus Valley to the Near East.

Procurement, External Trade & Mesopotamian Links
  • Procurement Colonies: Established at Shortughai in northern Afghanistan near Lapis Lazuli mines, and at Badakhshan.
  • Mesopotamian Cuneiform Texts: Dating to Sargon of Akkad (c. 2350 BCE), they record trade with three key regions: Dilmun (Bahrain, Persian Gulf), Makan (Oman/Makran coast, source of copper), and Meluhha (the Indus region).
  • Trade Cargo: Exports included carnelian, lapis lazuli, gold, copper, peacock figurines, and ivory products in exchange for Mesopotamian wool, oil, and textiles.
  • Currency Absence: Trade relied on a barter system. Coins did not exist. Seals and clay sealings were used to secure trade packets.
Transport Technology & The Lothal Dockyard
  • Lothal Dockyard: A massive trapezoidal brick basin measuring 214 x 36 meters. Connected to a tributary of the Sabarmati, it featured an inlet channel, a spillway, and a wooden lock-gate system to maintain water levels during low tides, facilitating shipping.
  • Land Transport: Solid-wheeled wooden bullock carts (represented by abundant terracotta toy carts and clay wheel ruts in archaeological strata).
  • Water Transport: Flat-bottomed river boats and masted maritime vessels, depicted on Harappan seals and clay amulets.

masteryZone.q: Why did the Mesopotamians refer to Dilmun (Bahrain) as a 'pure' or 'clean' land?
masteryZone.sol: Dilmun was a peaceful mercantile transit port where merchants from different civilizations met. It lacked monumental defensive fortifications or traces of military conflict, earning its name as a blessed neutral trading zone.

masteryZone.q: Why were clay sealings crucial for long-distance commerce?
masteryZone.sol: They acted as security seals. If the clay sealing remained unbroken upon delivery, it proved that the package had not been opened or tampered with, verifying the merchant's identity and protecting cargo integrity.

masteryZone.q: Why did the Harappans establish a fortified trade post at Sutkagendor on the Makran coast?
masteryZone.sol: Sutkagendor controlled the maritime entrance to the Persian Gulf. By placing a fortified post there, the Harappans secured their maritime trade route and monitored cargo ships heading towards Mesopotamia.

masteryZone.q: How did the lock-gate system in the Lothal dockyard operate to facilitate shipping?
masteryZone.sol: During high tide, ships entered the dockyard through an inlet channel. At low tide, a wooden sluice-gate at the spillway was lowered to trap the water inside the basin, maintaining depth and keeping ships afloat for loading.

masteryZone.q: How do cuneiform inscriptions help reconstruct the trade relations of the Indus Valley?
masteryZone.sol: They list imports from Meluhha (timbers, gold, carnelian, lapis, ivory), mention transit points (Dilmun, Makan), and describe ships of Meluhha docking at Akkad, verifying direct trade contacts.

masteryZone.q: How did the Harappans transport heavy cargo inland across vast distances?
masteryZone.sol: They used solid-wheeled wooden bullock carts pulled by oxen. Fossilized clay wheel ruts matching modern track gauges suggest that these carts travelled along established, standardized land routes between cities.

masteryZone.q: Case Study: The Lothal Dockyard and Tidal Engineering. Analyze its design.
masteryZone.sol: Constructed in the delta of the Sabarmati, the dockyard shows advanced knowledge of tides. The basin was lined with thick burnt bricks to resist water pressure, and a lock-gate regulated water levels, allowing year-round harbor operations in a tidal estuary.

masteryZone.q: Case Study: Mesopotamian Trade Tablets. Discuss the textual evidence of Meluhha.
masteryZone.sol: Mesopotamian tablets from the Akkadian and Ur III periods detail trading contracts. In one tablet, Sargon of Akkad boasts that ships of Meluhha, Makan, and Dilmun docked at his capital, proving the scale of Indus maritime reach.

masteryZone.q: Case Study: Shortughai Trading Colony. Discuss its strategic positioning.
masteryZone.sol: Located on the Oxus River in northern Afghanistan, Shortughai was isolated from the Indus plain. However, it was located near the richest lapis lazuli mines of Badakhshan and copper mines, serving as a dedicated resource extraction colony.

masteryZone.q: Teach the Concept: Sluice-Gate Hydrology in Lothal Dockyard.
masteryZone.sol: Explain how Harappan engineers used the force of gravity and wooden gates to trap tidal water inside a brick basin. This ensured that despite 4-meter tide variations, ships remained stable and floating during loading.

masteryZone.q: Teach the Concept: Tamper-Evident Clay Sealings in Ancient Commerce.
masteryZone.sol: Explain to students that clay sealings acted as a physical security key. If a sealing arrived broken, it indicated theft or tampering, allowing ancient merchants to secure trade caravans without metal padlocks.

masteryZone.q: Teach the Concept: The Meluhha-Mesopotamia Maritime Trade Route.
masteryZone.sol: Teach the route taken by Harappan ships: coast-hugging from the Indus delta along the Makran coast (Makan/Oman), stopping at Bahrain (Dilmun), and entering the Euphrates-Tigris delta to reach Akkad in Mesopotamia.

traps.title: UPSC Warning Alerts (Traps to Avoid)
items: Trap 1: Do not confuse Khetri copper with tin. Copper was sourced from the Khetri mines of Rajasthan (and Oman), while tin was imported from Afghanistan and Iran to alloy copper into bronze.

Trap 2: Watch out for statements claiming canal irrigation was common. Inside the main alluvial valleys of the Indus and Ghaggar, canal traces are absent. The only clear canals are found at Shortughai in Afghanistan.

Trap 3: Do not assume the Harappan economy was based on monetary currency. Metal coinage did not exist; trade was carried out purely through barter, facilitated by seals and sealings for cargo security and authentication.

Trap 4: Be careful with statements about the horse. While horse bones are found at Surkotada, the horse is NOT depicted on seals, and there is no evidence of horse-drawn chariots. The economy was powered by humped bulls and bullock carts.
Trap 5: Do not select options identifying iron as a trade commodity. Iron was unknown to the Harappans; it was only introduced during the Later Vedic Period (c. 1000 BCE).

practiceQuestions.q: Which of the following sites has yielded the most direct evidence of a ploughed field showing grid furrows indicating double-cropping during the Mature Harappan phase?
practiceQuestions.sol: Kalibangan in Rajasthan has yielded a ploughed field with grid-patterned furrows, suggesting double-cropping (mustard and chickpea/horse gram) during the Harappan period. Banawali yielded terracotta models of ploughs.

practiceQuestions.q:
Terracotta models of ploughs have been discovered at which of the following Harappan sites?
1. Banawali
2. Kalibangan
3. Bahawalpur (Jawaiwala)
Select the correct answer using the code given below:
practiceQuestions.sol: Terracotta models of ploughs have been found at Banawali (Haryana) and at sites in Cholistan/Bahawalpur (like Jawaiwala). Kalibangan yielded the actual ploughed field, not the terracotta models of ploughs.

practiceQuestions.q: With reference to Harappan agriculture, the term 'Sindon' referred to which of the following crops?
practiceQuestions.sol: The Greeks called cotton 'Sindon', which is derived from 'Sindhu' (the Indus region), since the Harappans were the earliest people in the world to cultivate cotton.

practiceQuestions.q:
Consider the following statements regarding the irrigation system of the Indus Valley Civilisation:
1. Direct traces of canals have been recovered from the site of Shortughai in northern Afghanistan.
2. Alluvial plains of Punjab and Sindh show a dense network of brick-lined masonry canals.
Which of the statements given above is/are correct?
practiceQuestions.sol: Statement 1 is correct: traces of canals have been found at Shortughai (Afghanistan). Statement 2 is incorrect: brick-lined canals are absent in the Indus plains of Punjab and Sindh. It is believed that siltation filled up any ancient canals there, or agriculture relied primarily on inundation and wells.

practiceQuestions.q:
Which of the following animals were domesticated by the Harappans?
1. Humped Cattle (Zebu)
2. Water Buffalo
3. Ass and Camel
4. Elephants
Select the correct answer using the code given below:
practiceQuestions.sol: All four animals were domesticated or known/exploited by the Harappans. Humped cattle (zebu), water buffalo, ass, camel, and elephant bone and artistic evidence are widely recorded in Mature Harappan levels.

practiceQuestions.q:
With reference to the horse in the Indus Valley Civilisation, consider the following statements:
1. The horse was frequently depicted on Harappan seals and painted pottery.
2. Skeletal remains of a horse have been identified at the site of Surkotada in Gujarat.
Which of the statements given above is/are correct?
practiceQuestions.sol: Statement 1 is incorrect: the horse is never depicted on seals or painted pottery. Statement 2 is correct: Surkotada in Gujarat has yielded controversial horse bones, but the horse was not a central part of Harappan economic or cultural life.

practiceQuestions.q: At which of the following Harappan sites were massive stone-cut water reservoirs discovered to manage seasonal dryland agriculture?
practiceQuestions.sol: Dholavira in Gujarat features large stone-cut reservoirs designed to collect and store rain runoff, representing a sophisticated system of water management in a semi-arid zone.

practiceQuestions.q: Which crop's husks have been found embedded in pottery clay at Lothal and Rangpur, showing localized cultivation?
practiceQuestions.sol: Lothal and Rangpur have yielded rice husks and fragments embedded in pottery, indicating localized rice cultivation in Gujarat, whereas wheat and barley were the primary staples in the northern regions.

practiceQuestions.q: The stone dams known as 'Gabarbands' were constructed to check water flow for agriculture in which region of the Indus Valley Civilisation?
practiceQuestions.sol: Gabarbands are stone-walled dams built across watercourses in Baluchistan to slow down surface runoff and deposit fertile silt on agricultural fields.

practiceQuestions.q: Which of the following statements is correct regarding the procurement of copper by the Harappans?
opts: Copper was imported exclusively from Mesopotamia.
Copper was sourced locally from the Khetri mines of Rajasthan and also imported from Oman.
Copper was sourced from Shortughai in Afghanistan.
Copper was not alloyed with tin during the Mature Harappan phase.
practiceQuestions.sol: Harappans procured copper from the Khetri mines of Rajasthan and also imported it from Makan (Oman). Chemical analyses of Harappan and Omani copper show traces of nickel, confirming a common origin.

practiceQuestions.q: With reference to Harappan bead-making industries, which of the following sites had specialized workshops?
practiceQuestions.sol: Chanhudaro and Lothal were major centers for bead-making, equipped with specialized bead drills, kilns for heating carnelian, and raw stone nodules.

practiceQuestions.q: Nageshwar and Balakot were highly specialized Harappan centers for the production of which of the following crafts?
practiceQuestions.sol: Both Nageshwar and Balakot are coastal sites that specialized in shell-working, including the manufacture of shell bangles, ladles, and inlay pieces, which were distributed inland.

practiceQuestions.q:
Consider the following statements regarding the metallurgy of the Harappan Civilisation:
1. The Harappans mastered the technology of smelting iron to make heavy implements.
2. Tin was alloyed with copper to manufacture bronze tools like axes and chisels.
Which of the statements given above is/are correct?
practiceQuestions.sol: Statement 1 is incorrect: Iron was completely unknown to the Harappans. Statement 2 is correct: Tin was imported from Afghanistan and alloyed with copper to make bronze implements.

practiceQuestions.q: From where did the Harappans import tin to alloy with copper for making bronze?
practiceQuestions.sol: Tin was a rare metal in the subcontinent and was imported from Afghanistan and Central Asia/Iran to alloy with locally procured copper to manufacture bronze.

practiceQuestions.q: Which material was used to make the standard, highly precise, cubical weights of the Indus Valley Civilisation?
practiceQuestions.sol: Standard Harappan weights were made of chert, a fine-grained silica stone. They were cubical, unmarked, and polished to high standards of accuracy.

practiceQuestions.q:
With reference to the Harappan weight system, consider the following statements:
1. The system followed a purely binary scale for all weight categories.
2. For higher values, the weight system transitioned into a decimal scale.
Which of the statements given above is/are correct?
practiceQuestions.sol: Statement 1 is incorrect: the binary scale (1, 2, 4, 8, 16, 32, 64) was used for lower weights, but it transitioned into decimal fractions (160, 200, 320, 640, 1600, etc.) for higher denominations. Statement 2 is correct.

practiceQuestions.q: An ivory scale showing divisions of linear measurement was discovered at which of the following Harappan sites?
practiceQuestions.sol: An ivory scale was discovered at Mohenjo-daro. A shell scale was found at Lothal, and a bronze scale at Harappa, demonstrating a standardized system of linear measurement.

practiceQuestions.q:
With reference to the trade colony of Shortughai, consider the following statements:
1. It was established in northern Afghanistan by the Harappans.
2. Its primary function was to secure the supply of Lapis Lazuli.
Which of the statements given above is/are correct?
practiceQuestions.sol: Both statements are correct. Shortughai was a Harappan trading outpost established in Badakhshan, northern Afghanistan, to exploit and control the procurement of precious Lapis Lazuli.

practiceQuestions.q: In Mesopotamian cuneiform inscriptions dating to Sargon of Akkad, the term 'Meluhha' refers to which geographical region?
practiceQuestions.sol: Mesopotamian cuneiform texts refer to the Indus Valley region as 'Meluhha', while Dilmun refers to Bahrain, and Makan refers to Oman/Makran coast.

practiceQuestions.q: The cuneiform inscriptions refer to 'Dilmun' as a land of trade. Dilmun is identified with which modern region?
practiceQuestions.sol: Dilmun is identified with the island of Bahrain in the Persian Gulf, which served as an important maritime transshipment point between Mesopotamia and India.

practiceQuestions.q: Mesopotamian texts describe Makan (or Magan) as a major source of which of the following commodities imported by them?
practiceQuestions.sol: Makan is identified with Oman/Makran coast, and was celebrated in Mesopotamian cuneiform records as a major source of copper.

practiceQuestions.q:
With reference to the Lothal dockyard, which of the following statements is/are correct?
1. It was a massive basin of baked bricks connected to a tributary of the Sabarmati River.
2. It featured a lock-gate mechanism to control water levels during tides.
Select the correct answer using the code given below:
practiceQuestions.sol: Both statements are correct. Lothal's dockyard was a highly advanced tidal dock made of kiln-burnt bricks, featuring an inlet channel and a wooden lock-gate to regulate water levels for ships.

practiceQuestions.q: What was the main medium of exchange in Harappan trade?
opts: Barter system based on exchange of goods
practiceQuestions.sol: The Harappan economy did not have metallic coinage. Trade was carried out entirely through the barter system, facilitated by standardized weights and measures.

practiceQuestions.q:
Which of the following archaeological findings suggests that the Harappans engaged in long-distance maritime transport?
1. Representations of masted ships on seals and amulets
2. Terracotta models of boats at Lothal
3. Traces of Indus-style seals in Mesopotamia
Select the correct answer using the code given below:
practiceQuestions.sol: All three findings support Harappan maritime activity. Representations of boats/ships on seals, terracotta boat models at Lothal, and Harappan seals found in Mesopotamian excavations confirm maritime trade links.

practiceQuestions.q: Where did the Harappans procure Lapis Lazuli from?
practiceQuestions.sol: Lapis Lazuli, a prized blue semi-precious stone, was procured from the Badakhshan region of Afghanistan, where the Harappans established a colony at Shortughai.

practiceQuestions.q: With reference to Harappan pottery and its economic role, which of the following statements is correct?
opts: Harappan pottery was exclusively hand-modeled and coarse.
Red-and-black painted pottery was mass-produced on wheels for domestic and export storage.
Pottery was painted using iron oxide base and white gypsum patterns.
Pottery was not used for transport of commercial goods.
practiceQuestions.sol: Harappan pottery was mostly wheel-made and mass-produced. The red-and-black painted jars were used as storage jars for trade goods like wine or oil, and have been found in Oman (Makan).

practiceQuestions.q: Which of the following semi-precious stones was sourced from Gujarat (Bharuch/Lothal) for bead-making?
practiceQuestions.sol: Carnelian, a beautiful red-orange chalcedony stone, was sourced from Gujarat (Ratanpur near Bharuch) and processed into beads at Lothal and Chanhudaro.

practiceQuestions.q:
Which of the following statements is/are correct regarding the transport system of the Harappan Civilisation?
1. Solid-wheeled wooden bullock carts were the primary means of inland transport.
2. Clay wheel ruts matching modern track gauges have been excavated at several sites.
Select the correct answer using the code given below:
practiceQuestions.sol: Both statements are correct. Terracotta toy cart models and fossilized clay wheel ruts matching modern gauges confirm that wooden bullock carts were standard land transport.

practiceQuestions.q:
Consider the following pairs of raw materials and their primary procurement areas in Harappan times:
1. Gold : Karnataka (Kolar)
2. Lapis Lazuli : Afghanistan (Shortughai)
3. Steatite : Southern Rajasthan and Gujarat
4. Carnelian : Gujarat (Lothal)
Which of the pairs given above are correctly matched?
practiceQuestions.sol: All four pairs are correctly matched. Gold came from Southern India (Kolar); Lapis Lazuli from Badakhshan (Shortughai); Steatite from Rajasthan/Gujarat; Carnelian from Gujarat.

practiceQuestions.q: In the Harappan weight system, the unit value of the key standard weight (corresponding to the 16th multiple) was approximately equal to:
practiceQuestions.sol: The unit standard weight (binary ratio 16) was equivalent to approximately 13.63 grams, which served as the baseline for everyday commercial exchanges.

practiceQuestions.q:
Consider the following statements regarding the role of seals and sealings in Harappan commerce:
1. A sealing was created by pressing a seal onto wet clay placed over knots of trade bundles.
2. If the cargo arrived with its clay sealing intact, it proved that the goods had not been tampered with.
Which of the statements given above is/are correct?
practiceQuestions.sol: Both statements are correct. Seals were not currency, but security devices. The sealing (imprint on wet clay) secured trade packages and authenticated the sender.

practiceQuestions.q: Which of the following sites has yielded a scale made of shell, used for linear measurements?
practiceQuestions.sol: A scale made of shell was discovered at Lothal. An ivory scale was found at Mohenjo-daro, and a bronze scale at Harappa.

practiceQuestions.q: Faience, a glassy glazed material manufactured from silica and gum, was primarily used for making what in the Harappan economy?
practiceQuestions.sol: Faience was a high-status, difficult-to-make material. It was used to craft luxury items like small perfume bottles, beads, and amulets, representing elite consumption.

practiceQuestions.q: Which of the following states was the primary source of Steatite (soapstone) used to manufacture thousands of Harappan seals?
practiceQuestions.sol: Steatite was sourced primarily from Rajasthan and northern Gujarat, which are rich in soft soapstone deposits.

practiceQuestions.q:
Consider the following statements regarding Harappan agricultural tools:
1. Wooden ploughs were likely used, which decayed over time in the alluvial soil.
2. Sickles made of iron were used for harvesting wheat and barley crops.
Which of the statements given above is/are correct?
practiceQuestions.sol: Statement 1 is correct: Harappans used wooden ploughs (as indicated by terracotta models). Statement 2 is incorrect: Iron sickles did not exist, as iron was unknown. They used stone blades mounted on wooden handles for harvesting.

practiceQuestions.q: With reference to the Indus Valley Civilisation, which of the following sites shows evidence of maritime contacts with the Persian Gulf through the discovery of a circular button seal?
practiceQuestions.sol: Lothal has yielded a circular 'Persian Gulf' button seal, confirming direct maritime trade contacts between Gujarat, Bahrain, and the Persian Gulf.

practiceQuestions.q: Mesopotamian cuneiform records refer to Meluhha as a land of 'exotic birds'. Which bird is commonly identified with this description?
practiceQuestions.sol: The texts mention the 'Haja-bird' of Meluhha, which historians identify as the peacock, known for its beautiful plumage and calls.

practiceQuestions.q: Which of the following statements about the craft of seal-making in the Harappan economy is correct?
opts: Seals were cast in bronze molds.
Seals were hand-carved in intaglio on soft steatite and then kiln-fired.
Agate seals were the most common type.
Seals were exclusively manufactured at Harappa.
practiceQuestions.sol: Seals were carved in reverse (intaglio) on soft steatite blocks. After carving, they were heated in kilns to dehydrate the talc, turning it into hard white enstatite.

practiceQuestions.q: With reference to Harappan textile industries, what was the primary source of dye used for coloring fabrics?
practiceQuestions.sol: Traces of red dye on cotton fragments suggest the use of madder, a vegetable root dye, demonstrating an advanced knowledge of dyeing textiles.

practiceQuestions.q:
Which of the following factors contributed to the centralization and standardization of the Mature Harappan economy?
1. Uniform weights and measures based on chert standards
2. Standardized brick sizes in the ratio 1:2:4
3. Centralized procurement colonies like Shortughai
Select the correct answer using the code given below:
practiceQuestions.sol: All three factors contributed to economic integration and centralization across the vast Harappan territory.

practiceQuestions.q: Which of the following is correct about the animal bones found at Harappan sites?
opts: Wild animal bones like deer and boar are completely absent.
Bones of cattle, sheep, and goat indicate they were used for meat and draft labor.
No fish or fowl bones have been recovered.
Bones of domestic animals show they were only used for religious sacrifices.
practiceQuestions.sol: Bones of cattle, sheep, goats, and buffaloes are common at Harappan sites, indicating their central role in the agricultural and pastoral economy for meat, milk, and draft work.

practiceQuestions.q: Jade, a green semi-precious stone used in Harappan jewelry, was imported from which region?
practiceQuestions.sol: Jade was imported from Central Asia or the Pamir region, reflecting the long-distance overland trade connections of the Harappans.

practiceQuestions.q: Silver ornaments were manufactured by the Harappans. Where did they source silver from?
practiceQuestions.sol: Silver was imported from Afghanistan and Iran, as it was not widely available locally in the Indus Valley plains.

practiceQuestions.q: Which coastal Harappan site in Sindh served as an export base near the Indus mouth, specializing in shell objects?
practiceQuestions.sol: Balakot was a coastal settlement specializing in shell-craft production and located near the mouth of the Windar River, serving as a maritime hub.

practiceQuestions.q: The Westernmost outpost of the Indus Valley Civilisation, which served as a fortified trade post on the Makran coast near Iran, is:
practiceQuestions.sol: Sutkagendor on the Makran coast was the westernmost Harappan site, functioning as a fortified trading post to monitor maritime traffic entering the Persian Gulf.

practiceQuestions.q: With reference to the decline of the Harappan trade economy in the Late Harappan phase, which of the following occurred?
opts: Weights and measures became even more strictly standardized.
Long-distance trade networks collapsed, and weights became localized and non-uniform.
Iron coinage was introduced to replace barter.
practiceQuestions.sol: During the Late Harappan phase (after 1900 BCE), long-distance trade with Mesopotamia collapsed, standard chert weights disappeared, and regionalized barter systems returned.

practiceQuestions.q: What was the main purpose of the spillway in the Lothal dockyard?
opts: To import drinking water to the town
To allow excess water to escape and prevent flooding of the dock walls
To act as a passage for small fishing boats
To clean the silt from the dock basin manually
practiceQuestions.sol: The spillway was a channel equipped with a sliding gate that allowed excess water to escape during high tides or floods, maintaining a constant water level in the dock.

practiceQuestions.q: Which of the following raw materials was sourced from the Nilgiri hills of Southern India?
practiceQuestions.sol: Gold was sourced from Southern India, particularly the Kolar/Nilgiri regions, which were rich in alluvial and vein gold.

practiceQuestions.q: Which site is known as a manufacturing hub for microscopic steatite beads, a highly specialized craft of the Harappans?
practiceQuestions.sol: Chanhudaro was a premier craft production center, famous for producing tiny, microscopic beads of steatite that required high technical precision.

practiceQuestions.q: Which of the following statements is correct regarding the double-cropping grid pattern of Kalibangan?
opts: The furrows ran parallel to each other in only one direction.
The furrows were cut at right angles to each other, with one set spaced closer and the other set wider.
The pattern shows that rice and wheat were grown simultaneously.
The grid pattern was constructed for drainage, not farming.
practiceQuestions.sol: At Kalibangan, the furrows were arranged in a grid, cutting each other at right angles. The wider-spaced furrows were for taller crops (like mustard), and the narrower ones for smaller crops (like chickpea).

mockTestQuestions.q:
Consider the following statements regarding Harappan agriculture and land tillage:
1. The ploughed field excavated at Kalibangan shows grid furrows, implying double-cropping during the Mature phase.
2. Banawali in Haryana has yielded the actual preserved wooden ploughshares used by Harappan farmers.
Which of the statements given above is/are correct?
mockTestQuestions.sol: Statement 1 is correct: Kalibangan has the ploughed field showing double-cropping. Statement 2 is incorrect: wooden ploughshares have not been preserved due to decay; Banawali yielded terracotta models of ploughs, not the actual wooden ones.

mockTestQuestions.q:
With reference to water resource management in the Indus Valley Civilisation, which of the following statements is/are correct?
1. Traces of stone-built dams or Gabarbands have been found in the Baluchistan region.
2. Massive, stone-cut rainwater harvesting reservoirs have been discovered at Dholavira.
3. A complex network of brick-lined irrigation canals is present throughout the Indus alluvial plains.
Select the correct answer using the code given below:
mockTestQuestions.sol: Statements 1 and 2 are correct. Gabarbands in Baluchistan and reservoirs at Dholavira are well-documented. Statement 3 is incorrect: there is a lack of brick-lined irrigation canals in the alluvial plains of Punjab and Sindh (only found at Shortughai, Afghanistan).

mockTestQuestions.q:
Consider the following statements about animal domestication and representations in the Harappan Civilisation:
1. The horse is the most frequently depicted animal on Harappan seals and copper tablets.
2. Bones of humped cattle, sheep, goats, and pigs are widely found at Harappan residential sites, showing their dietary importance.
Which of the statements given above is/are correct?
mockTestQuestions.sol: Statement 1 is incorrect: the horse is never depicted on seals; the unicorn is the most common animal, followed by the bull, elephant, etc. Statement 2 is correct: bones of domestic livestock indicate they were kept for meat, milk, and labor.

mockTestQuestions.q:
Consider the following pairs of craft specialization centers and their primary raw materials:
1. Balakot : Shell-working
2. Chanhudaro : Bead-making
3. Nageshwar : Steatite seal production
Which of the pairs given above is/are correctly matched?
mockTestQuestions.sol: Pairs 1 and 2 are correctly matched: Balakot was coastal and specialized in shell-working; Chanhudaro specialized in bead-making. Nageshwar is also coastal and specialized in shell-working, not steatite seal production.

mockTestQuestions.q:
With reference to the system of weights and measures in the Mature Harappan Civilisation, consider the following statements:
1. Lower denominations followed a binary system, while higher weights followed a decimal system.
2. The standard unit of weight was based on chert cubical weights weighing approximately 13.63 grams.
3. The system of linear measurement was completely non-standardized and varied between cities.
Which of the statements given above are correct?
mockTestQuestions.sol: Statements 1 and 2 are correct. Standardized chert weights followed a binary-decimal system. Statement 3 is incorrect: linear scales found at Mohenjo-daro, Lothal, and Harappa prove that linear measurement was highly standardized.

mockTestQuestions.q:
Consider the following statements regarding Harappan metallurgy and resource procurement:
1. Tin was sourced locally from Rajasthan to manufacture bronze tools.
2. Copper was imported from Makan (modern Oman) and also obtained from the Khetri mines of Rajasthan.
3. Iron was utilized to reinforce bronze chisels and saws for stone carving.
Which of the statements given above is/are correct?
mockTestQuestions.sol: Statement 2 is correct: copper came from Khetri and Oman. Statement 1 is incorrect: tin was imported from Afghanistan/Iran, not sourced locally. Statement 3 is incorrect: iron was completely unknown to the Harappans.

mockTestQuestions.q:
With reference to external trade as recorded in Mesopotamian cuneiform texts, consider the following identifications:
1. Meluhha : The Indus region
2. Dilmun : Bahrain in the Persian Gulf
3. Makan : The Oman Peninsula
Which of the pairs given above are correctly matched?
mockTestQuestions.sol: All three identifications are widely accepted by historians. Meluhha represents the Indus region, Dilmun represents Bahrain, and Makan represents Oman/Makran coast.

mockTestQuestions.q:
The Lothal dockyard is considered an engineering marvel. Which of the following features supported its functioning?
1. A massive wall of kiln-burnt bricks enclosing a rectangular basin.
2. A timber lock-gate at the spillway to regulate water level according to tides.
3. An inlet channel connecting the basin to a tributary of the Sabarmati River.
Select the correct answer using the code given below:
mockTestQuestions.sol: All three statements are correct. The dockyard featured a kiln-burnt brick basin, a lock-gate spillway for tidal regulation, and an inlet channel connecting it to the river to allow ships to enter.

mockTestQuestions.q:
Consider the following statements regarding the role of seals and sealings in Harappan trade:
1. Seals were primarily used as metallic currency to pay for imported goods.
2. Wet clay tags (sealings) placed over package knots allowed merchants to verify if a shipment was tampered with.
Which of the statements given above is/are correct?
mockTestQuestions.sol: Statement 1 is incorrect: seals were not currency; trade was barter. Statement 2 is correct: clay sealings served as security tags to detect tampering and identify the sender.

mockTestQuestions.q:
With reference to the trade post of Shortughai, which of the following statements is/are correct?
1. It was located in northern Afghanistan near the Kokcha River valley.
2. It was established specifically to control the trade of Lapis Lazuli.
3. It shows a complete absence of typical Harappan features like script and pottery.
Select the correct answer using the code given below:
mockTestQuestions.sol: Statements 1 and 2 are correct: Shortughai was in northern Afghanistan and controlled lapis lazuli. Statement 3 is incorrect: Shortughai was a typical Harappan settlement yielding Harappan pottery, seals, and script inscriptions.
